Worth remembering as a shape of failure: in this vault a sub-header without its own callout silently adopts whatever status is above it, and “silently” is the dangerous word.

voice.h4: One list (the second half of July 26)
voice.p: My Day and Today were two lists from two places that didn’t know about each other — one you curated on the site, one I wrote into the vault — and the one on screen had been carrying since July 19. Now they’re one. Every line of the check-in plan resolves to a real item id in the generator, so the plan can seed the list rather than sit beside it; you reorder and remove freely and your edits win; a new check-in stamp reseeds automatically, so eight days of silent carry-over can’t happen twice. Grouping is by pressure, not raw date — a hard external clock, then work that gates the set, then the undated. Pure due-date dividers were tempting and would have been a lie at 4 dated items out of 47: three rows and one heap. So dates got backfilled too — 25 of 51 now, and the ones still bare are bare on purpose, riding an addendum that has no date yet.

voice.h4: What the new machinery found on its first run
voice.p: Worth noting, because it’s the argument for building the plumbing at all. The Today→item resolver refused to bind one line — “Arrivals gate-lounge finishes” — which was strange, because the wording was identical to the item. The item was being read as **completed**: its group had no callout of its own and had adopted the Completed box above it. Same bug as the SME Workshop group found an hour earlier. Five live items in total were invisible. Neither would have surfaced by looking; they surfaced because something tried to use the data and failed.

voice.h4: My Day stops lying (July 26, late)
voice.p: Shadi’s objection was exact: “I can’t solve the full item, cuz I am waiting on info.” A list of whole items asks you to tick things that aren’t yours to finish, and a progress count built on that is fiction — it read 8/23 while most of those 23 were sitting in someone else’s court. Three changes. A **step can now be the row**: pin the single part you can do and ticking it records a step-done, the parent stays open. Every row **leads with the action** — the Next line or the step — with the item title demoted to a context line underneath, because the item title is not an instruction. And rows where the ball isn’t yours get their own **Waiting on someone** group with no checkbox at all, just a nudge button and how long it’s been quiet. Progress counts only what’s actually yours.

voice.h4: A render that failed in silence
voice.p: While wiring the step rows, one refused to draw — and nothing in the console. jsdom swallows exceptions thrown inside event listeners, so a broken render had been sailing through 141 green checks. The cause: I’d written `DETAILS[...]` where the global is `ITEM_DETAILS`, which meant the “Remember to ask” block built earlier today had been throwing every single time it ran and simply not appearing. Fixed, and the suite now installs an error listener and fails on any uncaught error — because a test that can’t see a thrown exception is a test that agrees with you.

voice.h4: Steps that read as one blob
voice.p: Second complaint, easier fix, same root cause: writing. Five steps on the riser-door item all opened with the same shape — “X — setting-out dimensions + mounting location; updated elevation” — so the eye had nothing to grab. They now lead with a verb and a number: SEND ① room names · SEND ② card reader · SEND ③ lift controls · SEND ④ room schedule · ASK Entro. Same treatment on the hardware, signage, evacuation and recessed-screen items. A step list is a scanning surface; if every line starts identically it isn’t one.

voice.h4: Two late captures
voice.p: **FRP at the staging areas, 4' above the staging room.** Logged as its own modelling item rather than reopening the closed staging-room finish plan, because the closed one says “walls at 4ft FRP1, P1-G3 above” measured in the staging *room* and this note is about the staging *areas* — so the reference level is genuinely open. I didn’t pick a reading; the item carries a CHECK step for the datum, because where the floor levels differ the band won’t line up and that’s a wall-tag problem, not a drawing tidy-up. It’s on the plan for Monday. **Retail screens.** It was logged twice — a strategy item and a recessed-detail item — which is why it felt unresolved: neither one owned the actual question. Merged into one. The whole thing is a single panel: metal, matching the adjacent ones, **removable** so a tenant can fit their own screen, and presentable when nothing is fitted. Strategy first, then detail-versus-note.

voice.h4: The screens were decided; their bulkheads weren’t
voice.p: Third late capture, and the most telling. The knuckle screen decision closed on Jul 16 — bulkhead removed, large screen onto the 16:9 canvas. The hammerhead screen is in the model with its detailing deliberately deferred to TP5 Addendum 1. Both *decisions* were tracked. The **bulkheads that physically carry those screens** were tracked nowhere, and neither was the 2D detail. That’s the gap a decision log leaves behind: closing a decision feels like closing the work. One item now, three steps — draw the detail, model the knuckle bulkhead, model the hammerhead bulkhead — hanging off Tuesday’s Latronics call with Marielle for mounting requirements.

voice.h4: The above-ceiling thread
voice.p: Four questions arrived looking separate and turned out to be one: what colour goes above the ceiling line, whether above the WC ceiling matches it, what the exposed gypsum actually is at the knuckle, hammerhead and art area, and whether the Nursing room entrance can be suspended gypsum instead of CM-2. They’re the same decision seen from different sides — the exposed face and the painted surface above the ceiling — and every one of them lands on wall tags before the 80% set. So: the baffle-top item widened to hold all three paint questions, exposed gypsum became its own item with a location per step, and the Nursing room got its own because it isn’t a finish question, it’s a ceiling-type recommendation with a detailing reason behind it. Building the Haptic agenda also turned up a ninth item that should have existed since Jul 17: when RFI-C-061 closed and the lower precast stayed, Haptic’s stone finish had to move to suit. It was written down as “new Pkg 5 action, Shadi to tell Anthony” — inside the closing note of the item being closed. Shadi’s answer when it surfaced: the wall already moved. So it wasn’t nine days unowned, it was nine days untracked — Haptic handled it and the vault never knew. Closed on creation, which is the right outcome and still worth the entry: the history now says it happened.

voice.h4: Untracked ≠ unowned
voice.p: Worth correcting myself in public. I called the knuckle stone finish “nine days, no owner” — it had an owner, it just wasn’t here. The wall had already moved. That’s a better outcome than the alternative and a useful distinction: a tracker that can’t tell the difference between work nobody is doing and work it simply can’t see will cry wolf, and then get ignored. The LED bulkheads were genuinely undone. This one was genuinely done. Both were invisible for the same reason — recorded in the closing note of a thread being closed — and that pattern is worth watching regardless of which way it resolves.

voice.h4: The map, and what looking for it found (July 26, evening)
voice.p: Shadi asked where a user should look first, and for a map he could hand to someone else. Answering it properly meant interrogating the data rather than the layout — and the layout turned out not to be the problem. Three of the Board’s four groupings collapse under real data: 112 of 137 items are Concourse B, 86 are Package 5, 36 of 54 open items are AR, and of 54 topics **37 contain exactly one item**. Grouping isn’t the useful axis here; pressure and ownership are. Two of the five headline numbers are things you’ve explicitly decided not to act on. And the tabs are nouns — Progress, Court, History — while the questions people actually have are verbs.

voice.h4: 39% of the record was never reaching the page
voice.p: Then the real find. History looked starved: 17 closed items with no story, 41 with no topic, half saying nothing. It wasn’t starved — the **parser was eating it**. Update lines were only matched as “YYYY-MM-DD: text”, but the house convention is “YYYY-MM-DD (capture): text” — every update names its source. 119 of 304 dated lines were silently discarded, and they were precisely the *attributable* ones: 70 captures, 20 check-ins, the Onware pulls, the named emails. So the site was showing the least sourced subset of the record and calling it history. Four date ranges (“2026-07-16/17:”) were going the same way. Fixed: 184 → 305 updates, silent closures 17 → 2, and the staleness triage halved because items only looked quiet on truncated history.

voice.h4: Knowledge, not labour
voice.p: So “what happened” now has two layers instead of one list. **Decisions** are marked explicitly in the vault — a `**Decision:**` prefix on the update that records the call — and gather into a record grouped by *thread*, never by date. Deliberately not inferred: “confirmed” means twenty different things in this project, and 26 items still read like decisions without being marked, which the health report now nags about. **Closures** carry a `✅ Settled:` line saying what is now true that wasn’t; 25 written, 58 still owed, and a resolved row in the stream now either states its settlement or admits nothing was recorded. Two more silent bugs surfaced on the way: the site’s detail rebuild whitelisted fields and dropped `settled` entirely, and the suite outgrew a single run, so it splits into halves now.

voice.h4: Threads, because the item was never the unit
voice.p: Shadi asked me to stop rearranging tabs and look at what the information actually is. The answer was in the shape of the data rather than the layout. **Nineteen percent of items here were explicitly split from, or merged into, another item** — when the unit of tracking keeps fissioning and fusing, the unit is wrong. And the knuckle bulkhead question spans five items over twenty-six days: no single item tells that story, but sorted by date the thread reads as one. So the thread is the unit; the item is the fragment a check-in happened to cut it into.

voice.h4: Why not person, package, place
voice.p: Person nearly won — 36 of 54 open items are, at root, waiting on somebody, which is the true shape of this job. But it spreads across 22 people and 15 of them hold exactly one item; person-as-home means fifteen folders with one thing inside. Package is one bucket (86 of 137 are Package 5). Discipline is one bucket (36 of 54 open are architectural). Place surprised me — half the items name a location, and knuckle, egress cores, retail band and washroom are genuine hotspots — but the other half name none and it fragments into nineteen places. Stage was the only axis that both spread cleanly and read *forward*: question → decided → drawn → queued → issued. Categories you have to memorise; a pipeline you can just follow.

voice.h4: A thread is a question, not a subject
voice.p: The change that makes it work is naming. `acoustic`, `floor-finishes`, `knuckle-bulkhead` are subjects, and a subject never finishes — which is exactly why 37 of 54 topics had drifted into singletons, collecting nothing and resolving into nothing. A thread is now named as the question it exists to settle: *what is exposed and what is painted above the ceiling line*, *is one evacuation zone acceptable and is smoke exhaust required*, *how does a tenant fit their own screen into our panel*. Questions have answers, so they have ends, so they have a stage. They live in a new Threads.md — which also means no item had to be re-keyed to gain one. Stage is derived, never written down, because a hand-maintained status is a status that goes stale.

voice.h4: TBB is not Concourse B
voice.p: Correction from Shadi. The TBB e-gates thread had been filed under Cross-program, which quietly implied it belongs to the same body of work as Concourse B — it doesn’t. It shares people and shares no scope. It now has its own program heading, so it can never inflate a Concourse B count or turn up in a Concourse B agenda. Small fix, but the kind that matters: a tracker that blurs two projects will eventually be used to argue about one of them with the other one’s numbers.

voice.h4: I never read the Sent folder
voice.p: Shadi: “doesn’t look like you went through my sent email.” Correct, and it produced the worst kind of error — the tracker told him to do work he had already done. The riser-door package went to Phoebe on **Jul 25**: the door/room/number spreadsheet with plans, the card-reader rule (300 max off the door, signage centred to panel), and the lift elevations. All four “SEND” steps were sitting open and dated for Tuesday. Worse, he asked Entro two questions back in that same email — does the C3.1 sign need 300 off the elevator door, and the back-face signs aren’t 1500 on centre, should they be — and neither was tracked at all. The court flips: Entro owes three answers before they pack the CD set. Reading only the inbox models a person as someone things happen *to*.

voice.h4: And Centralized is a different project
voice.p: Second correction in the same breath: Entro asked for the same room names on **Centralized**, and those have not been sent. Con B's went out Jul 25; it would be very easy to read that closure as covering both, and it doesn't. It's now its own item under Centralized / PBS with its own thread, precisely so the two can never be confused — the same reason TBB got lifted out of Cross-program an hour earlier. I couldn't find the originating request by keyword, so it's logged on Shadi's word with that stated plainly rather than dressed up with a citation I don't have.

voice.h4: Filed by subject, not by question
voice.p: “Why is signage grouped with door hardware?” Because I threaded it by its physical subject — the riser doors — rather than by the question it settles. Same doors, but: what hardware do they get is Steve Isaac's question on the hardware schedule's clock; what signage do they get and where does it sit is Entro's question on the CD-set clock. Two questions, two threads. This is precisely the failure the question-naming rule was written to catch, made by the person who wrote the rule, four hours later. Worth keeping visible rather than quietly fixing: subject-thinking is the default, and the naming discipline only works if it survives contact with a convenient-looking existing slug.

voice.h4: Evening check-in (July 26) — the Sent folder, again
voice.p: Three of tonight's four closures were verifiable in Sent before Shadi said a word: the elevator-cab depth answer to Chris Lenzin and Kevin Vogt (102 mm assembly, 53 mm into the CMU — that is the number structure has to accept), the ten-step YYC CAD export guide to the DT team, and Elisa's core height differences. Yesterday's standing fix is already paying. Two things got separated rather than closed: the fresh TP5 export going to Haptic tonight is the set they asked for, but sending it does not finish the review of their comments or the ownership split with Kirk, Luke and Michelle — so the send is a step and the item stays open. Same for NPS-C: the guide is written and sent, the files to SDS are not, and "done" meant the guide. Also caught: a Terminal Operations item tagged cat:: rfi with no number and no entry in the register — an operational access question wearing an RFI tag. Retagged.

voice.h4: The capture queue was stale
voice.p: Five of tonight's captures — the riser-door SEND steps and most of the My Day [done] marks — were already closed in the vault this afternoon. The browser is holding a queue built against this morning's upload, so the site is one regeneration behind what it is being clicked against. Nothing was lost and nothing was double-logged, but it is worth knowing the queue can re-report closed work: clear it after this upload.

voice.h4: Answers now land on the item (July 26, evening)
voice.p: A question you asked gets answered in a corridor, on a call, in a meeting — anywhere but this page — and until tonight there was nowhere for it to go except your head. Every My Day row and every open step in a drawer now has a ✎. It asks two things: what did they say, and what does that mean next. Recording it closes the ASK step, queues an Answered capture, and at check-in the answer is written onto the item as a dated **Decision:** so it joins the decision log and the thread timeline. Leave the follow-on blank and I'll propose one — an answer that doesn't produce a next step is usually an answer that hasn't been thought through yet. The item itself stays open: answers create work more often than they end it. First test of it is Monday: the Haptic pass carries ten questions, and every one has somewhere for its answer to land.

voice.h4: Filed under the portal, moved to flooring
voice.p: "Does the finish go below the portals" went in as a second question on the portal door-attachment stud, because the portal is in both sentences. Shadi corrected it: it is a flooring question. The stud item is about construction and lands on the portal detail; this one is about the floor plane running underneath and lands on the finish plan and the threshold. Different drawing, different consequence, different item — dated Jul 27 so it sits in Next 48 hours with the rest of Monday's pass. Third time today that a shared noun pulled two different questions into one place. The regression guard caught the unwind too: reverting the mis-filed step tried to delete a dated update, which is exactly what it is there to refuse.

voice.h4: Jul 31 is the Bid set
voice.p: The tracker has called Fri Jul 31 "the 80% set" since Jul 17 — Today header, milestone row, Protect line, addendum register, and every undated Pkg 5 item inheriting the date. It is the **BID set**, and there is no separate 80% milestone on TP5; it was folded into the Bid issuance. Nothing was scheduled wrong, because the date never moved. But the name is what tells you what happens to work that misses it: an 80% set implies a fuller submission still to come, and a Bid set does not. Corrected everywhere the name is load-bearing. Historical dated updates keep their original wording — they record what was believed then. One title kept its old wording deliberately: item titles are ids here, so renaming one reads as a dropped item to the regression guard and breaks My Day pins. The correction rides a dated update instead.

voice.h4: 42 quiet items, and 39 of them weren't
voice.p: The last check-in was Jul 26. Nine days later this page was reporting 42 items quiet past threshold and 27 of 28 dated items overdue — which reads like a collapse and was almost entirely an artefact. The board had been dated against the Jul 31 bid set, the bid set issued, and nothing got re-dated. Walking every item one at a time took the quiet count from 42 to 3. Worth remembering the next time this page looks alarming: check whether the clock moved before assuming the work didn't.

voice.h4: Addendum 1 has a date — September 25
voice.p: Eleven things were queued for an addendum with no date, which meant none of them could be planned against and all of them looked overdue-adjacent. Sep 25 fixes that in one move. It also means Addendum 1 work starts now rather than in September: the four RFI-PC notes PCL believes DIALOG owes, the nursing-room ceiling detail, the portal flooring note, the Arrivals seating/millwork/gates, and one correction that isn't optional.

voice.h4: The elevator lobby says gypsum
voice.p: Shadi found this by opening the issued package mid-conversation, not through any review process: the Departures elevator lobby shows gypsum where it should be CM-2. Arrivals is correct. That's not a drafting tidy-up — bidders are pricing the wrong ceiling. It's flagged high-impact and it goes into Addendum 1. Shadi's call was to treat it as isolated rather than trigger a full RCP-versus-schedule sweep; that decision is on the record, so if a second mismatch shows up the reading can be revisited rather than re-argued.

voice.h4: Two submissions, one Friday
voice.p: Aug 14 is Package 6.1/6.2 — and, as of this session, the YYC TBB submission too. Different projects, same day, Shadi coordinating both. Neither had tracked work against it: Pkg 6 had a confirmed date and an empty board because the design sits with Interiors, and TBB existed only as a Watch line that said Shadi wasn't an owner. Both now have real items. A package with a date and nothing under it is a tracker that can't warn you.

voice.h4: Four owed responses hiding in a Watch box
voice.p: RFI-PC-16, -18, -19 and -21 were sitting in the Addendum 5 Watch group with action:: review and a W badge — which this page renders as not-actionable — while PCL believed DIALOG owed all four responses. Nineteen days of quiet that read as 'nothing to do here'. They're Open now, court You, with a drafting step each. Same family of failure as the callout-inheritance bug: a status that hides work instead of describing it.

voice.h4: Two promises found in Sent
voice.p: The Sent sweep turned up two answers given with a promise attached and no item behind them. Jul 27, to Sam Rigby: 'Let me confirm and get back to you' about the mockups — eight days open, now paid and closed. Jul 31, to Sam again: '4 data and 2 power conduits… is my understanding' on the 98" displays, still unconfirmed with Electrical. An answer that contains the words 'my understanding' is an open loop wearing a closed answer's clothes. Two in one week is a pattern, not a coincidence.

voice.h4: P10 is black, P2 is white
voice.p: The above-ceiling paint question took three passes to land, and the first two produced codes that contradicted each other on the same surface. What it actually is: baffles P2 white, exposed gypsum below them P2, the first three feet of exposed concrete above the ceiling line P2, everything above that P10 black, and equipment above the baffles P10. Which means the Jul 17 record on this page — 'baffle underside matte black P10-G2' — was wrong, and is now marked superseded. Paint schedules get re-litigated three weeks later; that's the whole reason this log exists.

voice.h4: The connector was dark, and then it wasn't
voice.p: This check-in started with no M365 connector and no browser extension, which meant no email, no Teams, no Sent — the one failure mode that reliably produces triages telling Shadi to send things he already sent. We walked the vault anyway and wrote a check-list of what needed verifying. Then the connector came back mid-session and the list got worked properly: Matt Parks did stamp the drawings, Marielle's R1 AV files did land two hours before the set went out, S+A's sealed spec did arrive, and Andrea's 'all models are coming in at the old location' turned out to be TBB rather than Concourse B. Every one of those was a guess before the sweep.

voice.h4: Every thread on this page was nameless for a reason
voice.p: The health report has been saying 'threads have no question' for weeks, and the obvious reading was that Shadi hadn't written them. He had — Threads.md is full of them. The generator was simply never told where the file is: parse_tasks.py has a --threads flag and no check-in has ever passed it, including the command written into the pipeline skill. One argument took 60 unnamed threads down to 5, and those 5 were the ones created tonight. Now named too. The lesson is cheaper than the bug: when a report says content is missing, check that the content is being read before concluding it doesn't exist.

voice.h4: What's still owed
voice.p: Being straight about the debt rather than quietly carrying it. 44 closed items still don't say what they settled — down from 58, and the remainder are mostly June work whose outcomes aren't safely reconstructable, so they need Shadi's memory rather than my guess. 36 open items read like they carry a decision with no Decision: marker. Due-date coverage is 20 of 43, and it can't improve much until TP4.2 Addendum 5 and TP4.3 Addendum 2 get dates — six items are anchored to numbers that don't exist yet. That's the next clean-up, and it's a short one.

voice.h4: The Today block was doing two jobs
voice.p: First draft of tonight's plan had fifteen rows, which would have seeded My Day with a fortnight. So I cut it to five — and what I cut was the elevator-lobby CM-2 error in an issued bid set, the four RFI-PC notes PCL is waiting on, and Haptic's pending-items list that YYC is reading. Shadi's pushback was right: trimming important things to satisfy a count is a worse outcome than a long list. The actual bug was that the Today block is both the day's plan and the record of what a session found, those have different natural lengths, and it was the only thing seeding My Day — so the two were welded together. Now a line marked `[day]` seeds My Day and the rest render as the brief. Five on the plan, all fifteen still in front of you. Nothing was cut.

voice.h4: Three checks that would have caught tonight earlier
voice.p: The health report now watches three things it was blind to. A submission with a confirmed date and no items tagged to it — which is how Package 6 and TBB both sat invisible on Aug 14 for weeks. Items still dated on or before a submission that has already issued — which is the entire reason this page opened saying 42 items were quiet and 27 of 28 were overdue, when almost nothing had actually been dropped. And due-date coverage split three ways, because 'nobody set a date' and 'the addendum it rides has no date' are different problems and merging them hid the real one. The second check found five items dated behind the Jul 31 bid set on its first run. I had missed all five walking the board by hand an hour earlier.

voice.h4: Two of my complaints were wrong
voice.p: I listed eight improvements and two of them were me misreading the code. ★ HIGH already renders on the board. Waiting-on-someone rows are already excluded from both sides of the My Day done ratio, so a blocked day doesn't read as a failed one. Worth saying out loud rather than quietly dropping them — a review that only reports confirmed problems is a review you can't calibrate. The narrower real version survived: the addendum register rendered every row identically, so a priced error in an issued bid set looked exactly like work that only happens if a bidder asks. Those now show a ★ and an 'if asked' pill, and the card counts conditional work separately so an addendum can't look bigger than it is.

voice.h4: The pre-pull had been dead since July 31
voice.p: No pre-pull ran on the 3rd, and the reason turned out to be that the scheduled task did not exist. It had been created with the in-session scheduler, which does not survive the session ending — so it ran for a week and then quietly stopped, which is the worst way for a safety net to fail. Recreated properly, weekdays 07:45, and its first instruction is now to check whether it can actually read email and Teams and to put a warning at the top of the file if it cannot. That is the failure this whole session nearly shipped.

voice.h4: The Court tab was showing you your own work
voice.p: One argument in the wrong place. The chase list's guard read courtHasYou(it) where it wanted courtHasYou(it.court) — and String(item) is "[object Object]", which never contains 'You', so the guard never once fired. Every open item in Shadi's own court rendered as a person who owes him an answer, and because the groups sort by count, a phantom 'You — 29 items' sat at the top of the one view whose entire job is deciding who to chase today. It now opens on Chris Lenzin, who actually owes him three.

voice.h4: An eight-item addendum was reporting two
voice.p: The register collapses a task and its RFI-register twin into one line, which is right. It was collapsing anything that shared a topic, which is not — and six items ride topic addendum-5-4.2. So TP4.2 Addendum 5 rendered two rows, said "2 items", and hid four owed PCL responses behind a "+5 RFI twin" suffix. Those four are the ones this very session moved out of a Watch box for exactly this reason. Fixed the same night it was surfaced: a twin now has to be one line from RFIs.md paired with one from Tasks.md. The card reads 8.

voice.h4: Every evening the board moved a day ahead of itself
voice.p: Eleven places computed "today" as new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) — a UTC date. In Calgary that rolls over at 18:00, so from six in the evening until midnight the Upcoming view filed tomorrow's work under Today and today's under Overdue, the tab badge climbed with no change in the data, and the snooze picker silently refused tomorrow. One local-date helper, eleven call sites, plus a week-start function that had been landing a day early since it was written.

voice.h4: Package 6 had no card on the Progress rollup
voice.p: The rollup iterated the hand-maintained programs[].packages list; the Board appends whatever packages it finds on items. Those two drifted, so five packages — including Package 6, which has a firm Aug 14 submission and is half of this week's real risk — appeared on the Board and nowhere on Progress. The union of both is what should always have been drawn.

voice.h4: Two reviewers, and they agreed
voice.p: This pass ran two independent reviewers over the file — one on logic, one on what the data says that the interface never shows. They found the Court bug separately, with the same reproduction, which is the strongest signal a finding can carry. Eight fixes landed tonight. The rest is written down rather than quietly forgotten: the thread's own question never reaches the item drawer, "Completed this week" has been showing July for five weeks, the RFI register's age column is blank for seven of nine because it reads a ➕ tag almost nothing carries, and RFI-C-066 — the forty-one-day overdue blocking one — isn't in the register at all because it's written without a checkbox.

voice.h4: Three cards you flagged, three different bugs
voice.p: Screenshots beat descriptions. The thread cards said who holds a thread, how many items and when it moved — and never which package, which is the one thing you cannot infer from the rest of the card and the thing that decides which instrument the work rides. Added, with cross-package threads showing both names in a dashed chip, because a thread split across packages is a different management problem from one that isn't. The Flooring-at-the-portals card exposed the worse one: I folded decisions onto twelve items tonight and left their Next lines pointing at last Monday. All twelve rewritten. And the phantom "Addendum tp5-millwork" card turned out not to be a rendering problem at all — there was never a second instrument, only an unanswered question wearing one. Millwork rides Addendum 1. Closed.

voice.h4: A toddler toilet, and two things off the register
voice.p: New on Addendum 1: the Family WC needs a toddler toilet, and it is not in the issued Pkg 5 BID set. Court is Elisa Leung with Rick Baniqued alongside — Elisa first, so she is the bottleneck, and Rick is the natural second because the WC fixture families are his ask. Filed on its own thread rather than under wc-fixtures: that one is about updating families Rick requested, this is a scope question with a different counterparty and a different clock. Also noted on Elisa's card that she works out of Vancouver, which changes how you reach her. And the two `[Addendum –]` captures were a fair correction — the millwork question and the closed work-plan exercise were both tagged onto addendum registers, and a resolved question about which instrument to use is not addendum content. The register lists what has to be drawn.

voice.h4: Narrowing the seed wasn't enough on its own
voice.p: My Day came back with eighteen rows, which is how we learned that reseeding only ever ADDED. Cutting the proposal to five put five on top of last check-in's fifteen and read as twenty. Now a reseed also drops rows that only got there because a previous check-in proposed them and this one doesn't — and it says how many it dropped. Anything starred by hand is untouchable, because d.picked has always recorded the difference between what was proposed and what was chosen; the code just wasn't reading it.

voice.h4: The passenger bridge gets its own package
voice.p: It had been tracked as the second half of TP4.3 Addendum 2, and Shadi's read is that it probably needs its own instrument instead. So it moved out — its own section, its own Milestones entry, and both the package NUMBER and the date recorded as open questions rather than quietly filled in. Addendum 2 is down to the knuckle-core cut-and-secure and nothing else, which is worth knowing when that date finally lands. The closed work-plan exercise stayed in 4.3, because it genuinely happened there; only the forward scope moved. Same reasoning that kept the millwork addendum separate right up until it turned out to ride TP5 A1 — a scope with nowhere of its own to sit gets absorbed by whatever instrument is nearest.

voice.h4: Third time on the same rule
voice.p: Moving the item, I rewrote its title to describe its new home — and the regression guard caught it, as it caught the same instinct twice earlier tonight on the L17 item and on RFI 000104. Item titles are ids. The title still reads "the second half of TP4.3 Addendum 2", which is now false, and it stays that way on purpose with the correction in a note underneath. Three catches in one session is the guard doing exactly its job, and it is also the clearest evidence that the rule is genuinely counter-intuitive rather than merely forgotten.

voice.h4: An addendum is one instrument, several consultants
voice.p: DIALOG is responsible for architecture, but TP4.2 Addendum 5 also carries Mike Torjan's fire/smoke dampers, the M42.9.02 duplicate, Neil Dobie's three S+A items — hydronics zone matching and controls, the elevator sumps, and potentially some below-grade as-builts — plus the electrical knock-on from adding those dampers. All one document. The register listed them in one undifferentiated column, which meant the only question worth asking in an addendum meeting was the one it couldn't answer: whose items are still outstanding. New scope:: tag, and the register now groups by it — ours first with the amber edge, everyone else quiet but named — with a discipline filter for when you only want to see mechanical. Deliberately register-only; the Board is untouched. Add 5 reads 11 items: 5 architectural, 2 DIALOG mechanical, 3 Smith + Andersen, 1 SMP electrical.

voice.h4: Neil's elevator sumps are a commercial question, not a technical one
voice.p: His own framing is the useful part: "this could be an SI but I believe that PCL hasn't priced this yet and if we already have an addendum going out we might as well add it in there." That is filed as a decision rather than documentation, because the choice between an addendum and an SI is about money, not drawings — an unpriced item in an addendum gets priced with the bid, an SI is a change against a contract that's already priced. The below-grade mods came with the word "potentially", so they carry cond:: yes and the register shows them as "if asked" rather than committed.

voice.h4: Two honest corrections
voice.p: First: the ★ and the "if asked" pill I reported as shipped earlier tonight had in fact been rolled back by a script that failed on its last edit — the count line survived, the row markers did not, and I did not check. They are genuinely in now, and every edit since is applied atomically: validate every anchor first, write only if all of them match. Second: the smoke suite caught a real regression from this session's own data. Folding sixty dated updates in one day flooded the History stream's flat 120-event cap and pushed every closure off the first page, so the history tab showed notes and nothing else. The cap is per-type now — notes can crowd each other, they cannot bury resolutions. Resolved rows went from under five to forty.
